claims.title: Dithering boundary for finite-precision outcome renderers (systematic dithering, standard construction: Madow 1949)
claims.scope: per-trial outcome laws on a finite alphabet (Bell trials: K = 4) produced from tables of D-grid laws mixed by fresh per-trial private randomness; (a) unrestricted probability weights, (b) weights in (1/M)Z give exactly H_{DM}
assumptions: the private mixing index is drawn freshly and independently on every trial
part (a): mixing weights are nonnegative reals summing to one (at most K components); part (b): mixing weights lie in (1/M)Z
nonclaims: existence is immediate (point masses are D-grid laws); the content is locality, and the construction is Madow's systematic sampling (1949); no novelty is claimed for the rounding or dithering construction

a renderer that reuses one private draw across trials or uses a deterministic time-varying grid sequence (for example sigma-delta) is not covered; such schedules may be nearly indistinguishable from the base law
does not assert that physical randomness is or is not finite precision

claims.title: Commensurable-cosine Bell schedules cannot identify stationary finite precision under unknown visibility, for D divisible by 4 with c(v_max - v_min) >= 4b/D (single cosine: for even D iff [c v_min, c v_max] meets L_D)
claims.scope: Werner family P_v(a,b|s) = (1 - ab v c_s)/4 with v in [v_min,v_max] unknown, schedules whose cosines are rational multiples of one c (including canonical CHSH), stationary H_D renderers
assumptions: c_s = (a_s/b)c with integers a_s, common b, and D divisible by 4
c(v_max - v_min) >= 4b/D, or the exact single-cosine lattice criterion for b = 1 and even D
the setting rule is identical under both hypotheses
the precision D is declared in advance
nonclaims: for odd D, or D below the threshold, H_D and the Werner family can be disjoint; no separation rate is claimed there
the sketch's statement 'for every D divisible by 4 some v works' is false (counterexample D = 4, c = 1/sqrt2, v in [9/10,1])
does not say the Delft 2015 data were generated by a finite-precision renderer
composite Bayes factors with continuous priors on v are not claimed to equal one

claims.title: Settings 0 and pi/4: Theta(1/D^2) separation and Theta(D^4 log(1/eps)) trials (D = 0 mod 4, designs restricted to cosines in {0,+-1,+-1/sqrt2}); any quadratic-irrational ratio: Omega(1/D^2) separation
claims.scope: Werner family with v in [v_min,v_max], v_min > 0, schedules containing theta = 0 and theta = pi/4 (or any pair with quadratic-irrational cosine ratio for the lower bound), stationary i.i.d. H_D renderers
assumptions: v_min > 0 and D^2 v_min >= 1/(3+2sqrt2) for the stated achievability constant
converse: D divisible by 4, (v_max - v_min)D >= 4, and all used settings have c_s in {0,+-1,+-1/sqrt2}
achievability: fixed per-setting counts, n trials at each of the two settings
setting cosines are known exactly under both hypotheses
the precision D is declared in advance
nonclaims: only the order D^4 log(1/eps) is sharp, and only for designs restricted to cosines in {0,+-1,+-1/sqrt2}; the explicit constants differ by about 2.5e8
for a general quadratic-irrational ratio only the lower bound on separation is proved; no matching upper bound for D not divisible by 4 or for other quadratic irrationals
adaptive designs over arbitrary angles with unknown visibility are not covered by the converse, and adaptive allocation is not covered by the achievability bound
a cosine uncertainty eta >= 144/(sqrt2 (v_max - v_min)^2 D^2) voids the result (the Pell renderer is then an exact Werner law at an allowed cosine)
the Pell attainment is classical continued-fraction theory for sqrt2; the Diophantine inputs are standard

claims.title: Known-visibility finite precision: universal Omega(D) fixed-horizon converse, Theta(D log(1/eps)) with a D-adapted angle, and the sqrt2-digit law at a fixed angle
claims.scope: (a) any K-outcome base law, any setting set and any adaptive design with a fixed horizon; (b),(c) Werner law with v = 1 known exactly; (b) even D for the exact distance 1/D (odd D: 1/(2D)); (c) D = 2^k
assumptions: (a) the setting rule is identical under both hypotheses, fixed horizon n (or an almost surely bounded stopping time), D > K/4 and eps < 1/4
(b) cos(theta) = 1 - 2/D is set exactly and v = 1 exactly
(c) the single fixed setting theta = pi/4, k >= 3, eps < 1/4
setting cosines are known exactly under both hypotheses
the precision D is declared in advance
nonclaims: (a) is assembled from standard inequalities (largest-remainder rounding, H^2 <= l1, Bhattacharyya tensorization, Le Cam's 1 - TV >= BC^2/2); no novelty is claimed for the Hellinger converse
(a) is not a bound on the expected sample size of unbounded sequential tests
robustness of the adapted design to visibility loss of order 1/D is not claimed; a cosine uncertainty of 2/D voids (b) and (c)
the Ridout-based upper bound 4^{(1+e)k} is ineffective
IEEE-754 floating-point renderers are not H_D for any D; (b) does not apply to them, and nothing is claimed about double-precision rendering being detectable

claims.title: Binary digits of sqrt2 and Theorem 2 constants on declared finite grids
claims.scope: k = 3..64 for 2^k TV_k = 2||2^{k-3}sqrt2||; 110 declared D values up to 10^4 for D^2 g_D; all D = 0 mod 4 in [8,2000] for the Pell-multiple converse renderer; adapted design exact for D = 2^k, k = 1..12, and odd D in {3,5,7,9,15,33}
assumptions: nearest-integer branches decided exactly with math.isqrt; distances evaluated in 80-digit Decimal
g_D search uses convexity in m2 for fixed m1
nonclaims: the observed min_k 2^k TV_k = 0.01198 (k = 32) is not a lower bound for larger k
the observed D^2 g_D range [0.8368, 2.80] is not claimed beyond the declared grid

claims.title: Open rates for finite-precision identification
claims.scope: (1) fixed pi/4 with known v: is n_k = O(4^k log(1/eps)), equivalently inf_m ||2^m sqrt2|| > 0 (a classical open question; Borel's normality conjecture would imply a negative answer); (2) minimax trials with unknown v and free adaptive angles, between Omega(D log(1/eps)) and O(D^4 log(1/eps)); (3) J-setting and phase-nuisance rates
nonclaims: no rate is claimed for these cases
the J-setting separation exponent is a sketch, not a lemma
